artifact: MCR colistin resistance — primary-study harmonisation for the six largest seed rows
retrieved_from: Europe PMC REST (search resultType=core; fullTextXML where open)
method_note: Primary sources fetched by PMID; Ewers et al. read in full (PMC9780603, 224909 bytes). No number below is from memory.

six_largest.study: Liu Y-Y et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2016 (MCR-1 China)
six_largest.unit_note: N and n are SAMPLES (523 raw-meat + 804 animals + 1322 inpatients), not isolates
six_largest.detection: molecular (whole-plasmid sequencing + subcloning); prevalence by gene screening
six_largest.sampling_design: routine AMR surveillance of commensal E. coli, five provinces

six_largest.study: Chen X et al., J Med Microbiol 2017 (mcr-1 China)
six_largest.sampling_design: multi-province survey, 20 provinces/municipal cities; 2330 isolates of 10 species + 337 faecal samples
six_largest.host_or_sample: mostly farm animals; 229 human + 108 pet faecal

six_largest.study: Kawanishi M et al., AAC 2017 (JVARM Japan)
six_largest.years: not stated in abstract (continuous national programme)
six_largest.detection: gene screening for mcr-1 and mcr-2
six_largest.sampling_design: national routine surveillance of healthy food-producing animals (JVARM)

six_largest.study: Ewers C et al., Front Microbiol 2022 (porcine Europe)
six_largest.detection: culture; PCR for mcr-1/mcr-2; WGS of mcr-2 positives
six_largest.sampling_design: diagnostic-laboratory submissions - biased sample material (paper's own words; mainly piglets with post-weaning diarrhoea/edema)
six_largest.correction: numerator is 707, not 709; printed prevalence 10.42% is the study's overall rate (793/7614=10.4%), not Germany's; true 707/6158=11.48%

six_largest.study: Treilles M et al., Front Microbiol 2023 (goats France)
six_largest.detection: colistin-resistance screening; Southern blot; short-read + long-read sequencing
six_largest.sampling_design: targeted survey of breeding (n=80) and fattening (n=5) goat farms

six_largest.study: Walkty A et al., CMAJ Open 2016 (CANWARD Canada)
six_largest.detection: broth microdilution (CLSI) for colistin, then PCR for mcr-1 among colistin-resistant
six_largest.sampling_design: sentinel-hospital routine surveillance (CANWARD), consecutive clinical isolates, 1 per patient per infection site

ewers_table1_2010_2017_porcine.source: Ewers et al. 2022, Table 1 (PMC9780603); total 7614 isolates, 793 mcr-1 (10.4%), 12 mcr-2 (0.2%)
ewers_table1_2010_2017_porcine.note: per-country mcr-1 rows sum exactly to the study total 793

corrections_to_seed.correct: n=707, 707/6158=11.48%; the printed 10.42% is the study's overall rate 793/7614=10.4%
Spain n=16 (16/28=57.1%); NOT a duplicate of Portugal
Belgium mcr-1=11 (9.7%); 9 further isolates are mcr-2; seed's 20 = 11+9
primary-source sum is 793 (block is +12: Germany +2, Belgium +9, Spain +1); seed also omits the 'Other countries (32,0)' row

conclusion_for_item_23: On the six largest rows the reported sector gap is at least as consistent with detection method (gene screen vs resistance-first) and sampling frame (diagnostic submissions vs sentinel surveillance vs targeted farm survey) as with biology. Rows 6, 13 and 28 are clean and comparable and agree that human clinical carriage is rare while animal carriage is common - a real asymmetry of carriage that says nothing yet about cross-sector transmission.
limits: Collection years for rows 6, 13, 19 are not in the abstracts and were not pulled from full text this wake; marked 'not stated', not inferred.
Only the open full text (Ewers) was read in full; the other five were read from Europe PMC core records (abstract-level). A full-text check of rows 6, 13, 19, 28 is owed.
